content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to set up a password on a [product_name] so that when a user presses the escape button or navigates with up/down arrows, the [product_name] requests a password before allowing access to view the settings?
I don't think it's possible to require a password when navigating the menu on the [product_name] display. Password protection can only be applied to the program itself. Hope this helps.

My issue is that the [product_name] display shows the weekly timer settings. If the escape button is held down for a few seconds, it's possible to change these settings. I want users to be able to view the weekly timer settings on the display, but not be able to modify them.

Hello, You can enable protection in the weekly timer block to prevent modifications. Then, place the timer block parameters in a message block and apply protection to this block too. This way, settings are visible on the display but can't be changed by the operator—changes are only possible with [product_name] programming software. Regards,
Are you suggesting the settings should be entered directly in [product_name] programming software, by editing the specific block used in the program? Just a follow-up question.

Hello, Yes, once you protect the parameters in the block, they can't be edited on the [product_name] itself (parameters also aren't shown). Adjustments are only possible through the [product_name] programming software. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to prevent changes to weekly timer settings from the [product_name] display while still allowing these settings to be viewed. Current protection features block all changes but also remove visibility from the display, exposing a gap between parameter security and monitoring needs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want weekly timer settings to be visible on the [product_name] display, but editable only with proper authorization, ideally through password protection or a similar mechanism.
pain_keywords: inability to prevent edits while allowing visibility
